about: Generated by tools/map_layout.mjs from map/world/S1.json; never edit. Metres in the section frame: X east (out of the city in S5), D north, H up. Entities keep their map IDs; figures and trees also carry their slug as id for people.json.

assumptions: East-west and height 77 px per metre, depth 51.25 px of v per metre, as every section (S5). Things up the silk are painted smaller (questions: the diminution); positions come only from the map (BUILDING.md rule 5).

dx is S2's seam value, -51.6, held constant over the whole of S1 because no ground-level edge recedes anywhere in it (derivation). It is the painter's drift at S2's east wharf carried on, not a reading of S1.
Painted figure size is not a scale: S1's foreground travellers are 171-189 px tall (2.2-2.5 m at 77 px/m), 1.8 times S4's road figures, and the party's porters high up 80-115 px. Place by foot point.

The ground is one level (ground, H 0) everywhere it is not water: every bank, terrace edge and field line is a ground line at H 0. Each painted band is a bank one step higher to the north (35-90 px of face in the foreground, 5-20 px far up), and its rise is a build-time choice of the ground pilot (questions), not a frame height: the frame maps each stroke at H 0, so a bank top is placed as if it were level with its foot.

Water: the stream and the pale band (if it is water) are the support `stream`, H -0.7, measured at the bridge. A ground line drawn on the water's edge (a bank's foot that is the shore, the land tongues' edges) stands on `stream` (support_by, support), so the same stroke maps to one place; the near bank's top (the shores' shore_s) stays on the ground: the water at -0.7 lies 1.05 m north of it, the bank's slope between.
Riders: a rider's foot point is the ground under his seat (the units' convention), so his animal's support is H 0 and the builder seats him on the animal.

datum.about: where the route crosses the seam with S2 (u 29050): S1.road.main's centre-line point 0, exactly S2.road.main's last centre point (281.07, 16.29 m; scan (29050, 730), measured by S2; copied from map/strokes/S2.json by merge_fixes.mjs on every run). Station +314.87 there, S2's route station at that point (sections/canal/layout.json), so stations run on.

trees.what: A big bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) on the bank at the scroll's start: a thick gnarled trunk from spreading roots forks low into three main limbs, one rising north-west, one up to the crown's top and a long one reaching far east toward the silk's edge, all ending in crab-claw twig clusters; a short cut or broken limb stub juts from a limb at about (37235, 600). No leaves. A pole leans against the trees at its foot.

A tall slender bare tree east of the train: a thin dark trunk rising almost straight from the bank to a small crown of crab-claw twigs, whose limbs bend over and reach far west (slender form, like its card 2, 'a long curve to the west'); no leaves. The leaning pole S1.prop.leaning_pole_37075 rests across its trunk.

A big old bare tree (elm-like, elm_claw form): a thick gnarled trunk rises from roots spread over the stream bank at the small bridge's east end and leans north-west, forking at about v 700 into a limb up to the crown's top, a long low limb sweeping west over the charcoal train and a limb to the east; every branch ends in dark crab-claw twig clusters, no leaves. The donkey train passes behind (north of) its trunk.

A tall far tree painted in pale ink behind the big bare tree: a straight pale grey trunk and, at the top of the silk, faint wide fans of long fine straight shoots; a far willow with rising fans of shoots (willow_fan) or a pine-like tree (pine_fan). Bare or a faint haze.

A far tree near the top of the silk, painted in pale ink: from a head at about (36303, 310) fans of long, fine, straight pale shoots rise and spread over a faint short trunk. A far willow with rising fans of shoots (willow_fan, drawn small and far), or a pine-like tree (pine_fan). Bare or a faint haze.

Tall bare tree with a straight, slender dark trunk standing at the edge of the stream just west of the small bridge; it rises almost vertically, leaning slightly east, and forks near the top into a spreading head of crab-claw twigs, the highest crown of the three bare trees here (form elm_claw on a slender trunk); no leaves.
Far tree at the top of the silk behind the tall bare tree: two (perhaps three) pale fans of fine rising shoots (willow_fan far crown) spring from knobbly heads; its trunk is hidden.
Small far crown of fine rising shoots in a fan (willow_fan far crown) at the top of the silk, behind the bare elms; its trunk is not seen.

Big bare elm-like tree (form elm_claw) with two stems from one gnarled, knotted foot on the north bank of the stream (two dark knot-holes on the lower trunk): the west stem rises straight and bends over in a great arched limb; the east stem leans steeply north-east and crosses the trunk of the tall tree beside it; dark crab-claw twigs, no leaves.

Big bare elm-like tree (form elm_claw) with one dark, slightly twisted trunk rising from the north bank of the stream; at about two-thirds of its height it divides into an upright limb and long low limbs that reach far west over the slender grove behind it, all ending in dark crab-claw twigs with knobbly buds; no leaves.

Tall slender tree of the grove behind the bare elms (seven such trunks counted): a slender pale trunk, bare for most of its height, ending in a fan-shaped head of fine rising shoots (between trees/types.md `slender_3`, a young willow with a small head of rising shoots, and `willow_fan`'s far crowns); painted in pale ink (distant), early-spring bare.

A faint, rounded crown of fine shoots drawn in pale ink above the pollarded willow's fan: read as a farther willow (willow_fan, drawn small and pale) standing behind the farmstead, its trunk hidden by the willow and the roofs.

Pollarded willow (willow_fan form) beside the threshing floor: a pale, slightly twisted trunk rises behind the open shed to a big knobbly pollard head of several dark knobs (u ~35130-35290, v 590-680), from which a broad fan of long shoots springs up and out; on the east side the shoots arch over and hang down toward the floor. Early spring, bare or a faint haze. The largest tree of the farmyard's east end.

A small fan of long thin shoots drawn in pale grey ink, rising up and out to the north-west from a point just above the long farmhouse's ridge and the far roof's east slope: a far pollarded willow (willow_fan form, drawn small and pale for distance) standing behind the farmstead, its head and trunk hidden by the roofs. Early spring, bare or a faint haze.

The tallest of the farmstead's bare trees (elm_claw form): a straight slender trunk rising from behind the shrubs at the farmhouse's west end to a high crown of dark crab-claw twigs, with a crow's nest at the top (about (34680, 290)) and a second nest on a long branch reaching east over the farmhouse roof (about (34757, 350)). Early spring, bare.

Bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form), smaller: two stems from one foot, the west one curving up and slightly west, the east one straight, to a small crown of crab-claw twigs at about v 420-560 between the crowns of S1.tree.bare_elm_twin_34552 and the tall elm S1.tree.bare_elm_tall_34703. Early spring, bare.

Bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) with no leaves: two stems from one foot; the west stem leans and curves north-west to a crown of dark crab-claw twigs with a crow's nest (a dark tangled clump) at about (34445, 393); the east stem rises nearly upright to about (34525, 420) and spreads east. Early spring, bare. Stands just behind (north of) the ground line at the front of the farmstead, among the shrub belt.

A tall straight trunk drawn only in pale outline (two faint lines about 33 px apart, plain silk between), rising from behind the shrub belt to about v 490, where it disappears among the elm's twigs; no crown of its own shows. Read as a slender bare tree (slender form) standing a little behind the hedge, drawn pale; it could be a willow whose crown is lost in the faded silk.
A second, thinner pale vertical trunk line just west of S1.tree.pale_trunk_34474, from behind the shrub belt up to about v 495: a slender far tree (slender form), drawn very faint.

Bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) standing at the west edge of the farmyard: a straight pale trunk forking high (about v 390) into branches that spread to a broad crown of crab-claw twigs; a pale perched bird (?) sits in its crown (S1.ani.pale_bird_34250).

Large bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) at the east end of the big thatched farmhouse: a straight trunk that sends two long heavy limbs east, level over the farmyard to about u 34430, hung with crab-claw twig sprays (one spray hangs low over the yard at about 34250-34390, v 690-770), and rises to a smaller crown above.

Bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) with two stems from one foot in front of the thatched farmhouse: a near-vertical stem forking at about v 570 into a small crab-claw crown, and a long stem leaning north-east across the roof, crossing in front of the next tree's trunk at about (34025, 700) and rising to a fork at about (34010, 530) with its own crab-claw crown.

Slender bare tree (elm-like) rising straight in front of the thatched farmhouse to a crown that spreads up to the north-east in long crab-claw branches; a dark nest sits where its trunk ends among the top twigs (S1.prop.nest_33900).

The tallest tree of the farmhouse grove: a long straight slender bare trunk (elm-like, slender with a crab-claw crown) rising from in front of the thatched farmhouse to a small high crown of crab-claw twigs near the top of the grove.

Bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) in front of the long thatched farmhouse: one foot with roots spreading west, a short trunk forking low (about v 770) into two or three tall stems: the west stems rise and lean up-left to a crown of crab-claw twigs, the east stem rises up-right, then straight, to a higher crown. No leaves.

A faint, pale broad trunk with no dark outline standing behind the long thatched farmhouse between the two dark-trunked groups; a few small claw twigs at about (33690-33736, 553-607) may be its crown.
Bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) behind the long thatched farmhouse, its trunk drawn as two parallel contour lines rising to a rounded crown of crab-claw twigs lower than its tall neighbour's.

Tall bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form) standing behind the long thatched farmhouse: a straight slender trunk rising to a high flat crown of crab-claw twig clusters spread wide east and west, the crown reaching near the top of the grove. No leaves.
A faint, pale-inked far tree standing behind the westernmost thatched house: a thin pale trunk and a small crown of pale twigs, drawn much lighter than the trees in front (distance or mist).

Bare elm-like tree (elm_claw form), about 520 px tall: one trunk rising from the ground in front of the west end of the westernmost thatched house, forking at about v 620 into two twisting stems; the west stem bends up-left into a broad flat crown of dark crab-claw twig clusters, the east stem turns into a long limb rising north-east to a second crab-claw head; a short side branch with claw twigs at about (33430-33510, 570-625). No leaves.
Far bare tree (elm_claw): a straight trunk forking at about v 470 into two limbs, west and north-east, ending in angular crab-claw twigs, no leaves.
Far bare tree (elm_claw): a straight dark trunk rising to angular crab-claw branches with knobbly twig clusters, no leaves.
Small far bare tree (elm_claw, small): a short dark trunk with angular crab-claw branches spreading west and east, and one long thin branch rising to the north-west.
Far slender bare tree: a thin straight trunk with a spray of upright forking bare branches at the top.
Far bare tree of two thin stems from one (hidden) foot, each forking at the top into upright bare twigs (slender form).

Huge old pollard willow (willow_burl): a lumpy, dark-knotted bole with a root flare to the west, leaning east as it rises from the foot to a fork at about (32930, 1100); a west limb ends in a knobbly head at (32825-32900, v 1000-1080) and an east limb in heads at (32940-33085, v 978-1060); long bare whips rise to v ≈ 630 and sweep east as far as u ≈ 33410, their ends drooping to v 1050-1110. Early spring: bare. The easternmost of the great willows; open ink-wash ground lies east of it.
Far slender bare tree: a thin trunk with a second, thinner stem beside it, both rising to small forks of bare twigs.
Far slender bare tree: a thin straight trunk forking near the top into a few bare branches.
Very faint thin bare sapling (slender form) in the far grove, a single stem with a small fork at the top.
Far bare tree (elm_claw, small and faint): a thin trunk leaning west as it falls, under a flat crown of twisted horizontal branches with knotty twig clusters, no leaves.

The largest tree of the countryside: a massive, dark, lumpy and moss-dotted bole 150-200 px wide with exposed knobbly roots running east along the ground to about u 32845; the bole leans west as it rises to a broad knobbly pollard head of two or three clubbed knobs (u 32400-32600, v 930-1055), from which a fountain of long straight bare whips rises to the top of the crown (v ≈ 290) and spreads from about 32230 to 32790. Early spring: bare, the whip tips drawn in fine pale fans.
Far bare tree (elm_claw, small and faint) seen above the great willows' crowns: a straight trunk carrying a spreading crown of twisted, angular, crab-claw branches with no leaves.

Huge old pollard willow (willow_burl): a thick burled bole about 130 px wide at the foot, pale-barked between dark lumpy contours, leaning west as it rises; at about v 1100 it forks into two short limbs, each ending in a knobbly clubbed pollard head (west head about (32275, 1040), east head about (32345, 1015)), from which fans of long straight bare whips rise and spread west over the open ground. Early spring: bare, at most a faint haze. Stands just behind (north of) the great willow S1.tree.willow_burl_great_32620.

The largest of the great old willows: a huge dark burled bole, very knobbly, with big swollen burls on its east side (about (32040-32110, 1000-1080) and (32050-32120, 1210-1270)), rising slightly north-west to a clubbed pollard head at about (31930-32060, 840-940), from which a dome of fine bare twigs and whips rises to v 242; at its foot the roots spread like rocks east to u 32270 and west to 31960. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.

Great old willow of 隋堤烟柳, third from the west: a tall trunk leaning north-west from its foot, pale-barked above and with dark swollen burls in its middle (about v 1130-1300) where it presses against the burled willow to the east, rising to a knobbly pollard head at about (31800-31900, 930-1000) from which bare whips fan up into the shared canopy. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.

Great old willow of 隋堤烟柳, second from the west: a massive dark knobbly burled trunk rising from a foot shared with its western neighbour and leaning north-east, widening upward and dividing in its upper part into two knobbly stems (u about 31680-31700 and 31730-31800 at v 1000-1100), to a clubbed pollard head at about (31690-31800, 890-960) with a fan of long bare whips. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.

One of the great old willows of 隋堤烟柳, the westernmost of four: a massive pale-barked trunk with dark knots and hollows (one big eye at about (31576, 1166)), leaning north-west from its foot to a broad knobbly pollard head at about (31430-31560, 940-1000), from which long straight bare whips fan up and far to the west over the shed on posts, to about u 31150 and v 400. A small fan of young shoots springs from its east side at about (31610, 1040). Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.

Far pollarded old willow, the eastern and nearer of a pair with S1.tree.willow_far_31443: a heavier knobbly trunk to a clubbed head at about (31477-31537, 293-360), throwing fans of long bare shoots up and to the east as far as u 31820. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).

Far pollarded old willow on the ground above the great willows, the western of a pair: a short thick trunk to a dark knobbly head at about (31420-31477, 290-360), from which long bare shoots fan up to the silk's top edge, making with its neighbour S1.tree.willow_far_31505 one broad canopy over u 31250-31820. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).

A small slender far tree or sapling: a thin straight stem about 50 px tall with a short second stem or fork just east of it (u 31355-31360, v 360-390), standing on the far ground under the crowns of the far willows. Bare.

Far pollarded old willow at the top of the silk, beside S1.tree.willow_far_31190: an upright trunk to a knobbly head at about (31240, 165) with a fan of long bare shoots rising to the silk's top edge. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).

A great old willow at the east end of the thatched hut, leaning hard north-west: its huge low hollow bole (a broad mottled mass about 150 px wide with a dark round hollow in its east face) sits on the bank just south of the shed's fence, and its trunk runs up-left past the west end of that fence, in front of the hut's wattle fence and east gable, to a pollard head at about the hut's eave, from which bare whips fan up over the hut's thatched roof. Early spring, bare. willow_burl form.

Far pollarded old willow at the top of the silk: one stout trunk leaning north-west from its foot to a knobbly clubbed head at about (31145, 155), from which a fan of long straight bare shoots rises and one long limb reaches far west along the silk's top edge. Early spring, bare or a faint haze. willow_burl form, drawn small (far).
Far tree or shrub crown cut by the silk's top edge: a cluster of dark knotted blotches (u 30955-31015) like a far pollard head or a bush on the far ridge.
Far shrubs or small tree crowns cut by the silk's top edge: dark knotted blotches in a row along the edge (u 30830-30920), like the far crowns the painter dots along a distant ridge.

Willow of the willow_fan form, the east one of the pair: a slender dark trunk rising nearly upright to knobbly heads with fans of long straight bare shoots that spread east over the party's track; early spring, no leaf.

Willow of the willow_fan form, the west one of a pair standing 80 px apart on a bank above the chasers: a slender dark trunk leaning a little east forks at about two thirds of its height into knobbly heads that throw fans of long, straight, bare shoots up to near the top of the silk; early spring, no leaf painted.
Far willow (willow_fan, a far crown) up the slope north of the chasers' bank: a dark knobbly pollard head throwing a fan of fine bare shoots in all directions; its short trunk is faint.

A small far tree or bush on the far fields at the top of the silk: a dark stem slanting from its foot up to the north-west, with fans of fine twiggy branches spreading west and up to the silk's top edge, which cuts the crown. Bare, early spring; drawn small (far).

S1.veh.boat_sampan_36440.name: small empty boat (sampan) moored under the small bridge
S1.veh.boat_sampan_36440.what: A small open wooden boat (a sampan), empty: no crew, mast, cabin, sweep or cargo. It lies along the bank just south of the small bridge, a raised square end (transom) to the west and a raised pointed end to the east, with one thwart near the east end. A thin upright pole stands in the stream at its pointed east end (S1.prop.mooring_pole_36444): the boat is tied to it.

S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.name: willow-decked sedan chair of the tomb-sweeping party
S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.what: Sedan chair decked with willow (杨柳杂花装簇轿顶), carried west-south-west down the upper track: a tall, closed, dark box (its east side darker than its west face) with a low roof and a knob finial; a big spray of about 6-8 long willow twigs fans up and out to the west from the roof's west corner, more willow strands hang down its west face, and a few twigs stand at its east corner.
